prose-content dark:prose-invert max-w-none pt-4 pb-0"> <div class="o-guide" data-astro-cid-yteeqxyj><a id="introducing-o"></a><a id="what-is-o"></a><p>Your dot is an always-on agent that keeps work moving across your tools and projects. You can keep talking to it while it works, and it reaches out with results or decisions that need you.</p><p>Powered by GPT-6 Astra, your dot lives in the cloud and has its own computer and browser. You can reach it and it can keep working even when your computer is off. It can research, analyze data, prepare documents, and build software, using relevant context from past conversations and your preferences.</p><a id="access-to-dots"></a><p><strong>Dots are rolling out gradually to eligible accounts.</strong> See <a href="#access">availability and access</a> for plan, region, and workspace requirements.</p><a id="meet-your-o"></a><h2 id="make-it-your-own" Setup offers app connections and, in the desktop app, access to your computer. Your dot introduces itself and uses the context available to it to suggest ways it can help. You can start talking to it while it gets to know your work.</p><p>Give your dot a name and choose its shape, color, eyes, glasses, and accessories. You can change these anytime.</p><p>Your dot starts with a handle such as @yourname-dot. Naming it updates the handle, for example, @tibo-alfred for a dot named Alfred.</p><a id="make-it-yours"></a><a id="stay-connected"></a><a id="your-dot-wherever-you-are"></a><h2 </div><p>You can message your dot or call it to discuss work, change priorities, or make a decision. In ChatGPT, select the phone button in your dot’s conversation to start a call. You can also type messages while you’re talking. Work you’ve assigned can continue after the call ends.</p><p>You reach the same dot in ChatGPT, Slack, Teams, or a call. Changing where you talk to it doesn’t start a new dot or reset its memory. Messages stay in their respective channels, while your dot can use relevant context across them. Before sharing information from a private conversation with other people, your dot checks that you’ve allowed it.</p><p>Tell your dot where to send different kinds of updates. For example, ask it to keep routine progress in ChatGPT and bring decisions to you in Slack. Explain which changes need your attention, such as a deadline at risk.</p><a id="choose-where-o-can-reach-you"></a><a id="where-to-use-o"></a><p>Open your dot’s profile and select <strong>Add</strong> to connect an available contact method. See <a href="/codex/dots/channels">Message your dot</a> for channel details.</p><p>In Slack, you can DM your dot or mention it in a channel you’ve added it to. By default, it responds to you; you can instruct it to engage with others. Existing permissions and safeguards still apply to what it shares and does. Tell it which channels and events to watch for. Adding it to a channel alone doesn’t start monitoring. You can also message your dot in Microsoft Teams. See <a href="/codex/dots/channels#slack-and-teams">Slack and Teams</a>.</p><a id="how-o-works"></a><a id="how-your-dot-works"></a><h2 id="how-dots-work" class="group flex items-center gap-2 mt-7 mb-2 conversations. It tracks progress, works out what needs to happen next, and follows through as things change. Once you’ve asked it to handle something, you can return with new information or priorities without restarting the work. Your dot brings back results and turns to you for decisions that need your judgment.</p><div class="contents" data-markdown-export="illustration" data-markdown-description="A dot explains how it follows up between conversations and asks for decisions."> <figure aria-label="A dot explains how it follows up between conversations and asks for decisions." data-markdown-description="A dot explains how it follows up between conversations and asks for decisions." data-markdown-export="illustration" role="img" class="not-prose relative isolate m-0 w-full rounded-xl [container-type:inline-size] overflow-visible my-8 bg-white p-[clamp(16px,4cqw,32px)] text-[#202123] dark:bg-[#171717] dark:text-[#ececec]" style="aspect-ratio:957 / 596"><div aria-hidden="true" class="contents"><div class="mx-auto flex w-full max-w-[760px] flex-col gap-5 text-[clamp(14px,2.2cqw,17px)] leading-[1.5] tracking-[-0.01em]"><div class="flex flex-col items-center pb-1"><img src="/images/codex/dots/default-dot.svg" width="80" height="80" alt="" class="block size-20 shrink-0"/><div class="max-w-full rounded-[18px] border border-[#dedede] bg-white px-5 py-2 text-center shadow-sm dark:border-[#3c3c3c] dark:bg-[#212121]"><div class="text-[18px] font-medium text-[#6b6b6b] dark:text-[#ececec]">Your dot</div><div class="text-[13px] text-[#767676] dark:text-[#aaa]">Here to help</div></div></div><div class="text-center text-[12px] text-[#767676] dark:text-[#aaa]">Today, 9:41 AM</div><div class="flex flex-col gap-4"><div class="w-fit max-w-[94%] rounded-[24px] px-[clamp(16px,3cqw,24px)] py-3 break-words mr-auto bg-[#f3f3f3] dark:bg-[#2a2a2a]">Hi, I’m your dot. I keep working between our conversations.</div><div class="w-fit max-w-[94%] rounded-[24px] px-[clamp(16px,3cqw,24px)] py-3 break-words ml-auto bg-[#ffd34f] text-[#181500]">What happens while I’m away?</div><div class="w-fit max-w-[94%] rounded-[24px] px-[clamp(16px,3cqw,24px)] py-3 break-words mr-auto bg-[#f3f3f3] dark:bg-[#2a2a2a] rounded-bl-[9px]">I track progress and follow up as things change. I’ll bring you results and ask when I need your decision.</div><div class="w-fit max-w-[94%] rounded-[24px] px-[clamp(16px,3cqw,24px)] py-3 break-words mr-auto bg-[#f3f3f3] dark:bg-[#2a2a2a] -mt-3 rounded-tl-[9px]">Tell me what to watch for and when to update you.</div></div></div></div></figure> </div><p>Your dot can decide when to pause and wake up to continue work; you don’t need a fixed schedule for every follow-up. It can use background agents to work on several things in parallel while you keep talking to it. It also researches connected information to suggest useful next steps.</p><p>For example, if your dot is helping organize an offsite, it can update the headcount as people confirm and ask before sending a request for revised pricing.</p><a id="context-that-carries-forward"></a><h3 id="memory-and-context" class="group flex items-center gap-1 mt-7 mb-2 scroll-mt-[110px]"><span class="min-w-0">Memory and context</span><button type="button" class="shrink-0 self-center inline-flex items-center justify-center rounded-md p-0.5 opacity-0 transition-colors transition-opacity dot draws on the conversation, relevant ChatGPT memory, and its own saved notes about your preferences, decisions, and ongoing work. These notes carry forward across conversations and contact methods, so it can build on what you’ve discussed as your work changes.</p><p>It can also research connected information and keep private notes to identify useful next steps. That research is read-only; follow-up actions require the applicable permissions. See <a href="/codex/dots/tasks-and-memory">Tasks and memory</a>.</p><a id="where-the-work-happens"></a><h3 id="its-computer-and-yours" class="group flex items-center gap-1 mt-7 mb-2 Cloud work can continue while your devices are off. When you need to inspect the browser or do a step yourself, open its computer and select <strong>Take over</strong>. Select <strong>Return control</strong> when you’re ready for your dot to continue. See <a href="/codex/dots/computers-and-apps">computers and apps</a> for connection details.</p><astro-island uid="ZTuJ3r" prefix="r27" over</button></div></div></div></div></figure></div><!--astro:end--></astro-island><p>Connect your computer once through your dot’s profile to make its local files, code, and apps available for your dot’s work. You can connect only one personal computer at a time. The connection stays in place between tasks. Your computer must be online with the ChatGPT app open for your dot to use it. This permission is separate from connecting your computer to Codex or enabling Work Sync.</p><p>Your dot can use supported <a href="/codex/plugins">plugins</a> installed and enabled for your account, with their connected accounts and existing permissions. For example, use Gmail to find relevant email, Google Drive to work with documents, and GitHub to investigate code and prepare changes. Each plugin must be connected and permitted to perform the actions you request. Local skills require a connected computer. Connecting a messaging channel doesn’t automatically grant access to your apps or computer.</p><a id="connections"></a><p>Each connection serves a different purpose:</p><div class="table-wrapper md:max-w-5xl mx-auto overflow-x-auto"><table class="w-full">
<thead>
<tr>
<th>Connection</th>
<th>What it enables</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td>Messaging channel</td>
<td>Talk to your dot and receive updates there.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Connected app or plugin</td>
<td>Use that service’s information and tools within its permissions.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Local computer</td>
<td>Work with that computer’s files, apps, and tasks while it’s available.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div><p>Connecting a messaging channel doesn’t also connect your inbox, other apps,
or local computer. Your dot’s cloud computer is separate from your devices
and their signed-in browser sessions.</p><h3 id="signing-in-to-websites" class="group flex items-center gap-1 mt-7 mb-2 scroll-mt-[110px]"><span class="min-w-0">Signing in to websites</span><button as ChatGPT Work. When a website needs a login, it can send you a sign-in request. Open the request to enter your credentials and any requested verification in a private form. Your credentials go to the browser outside the conversation. class="_button_gbude_190 _submit_gbude_205">Sign in</span></div></div></div></div></div></figure></div><p>The cloud browser has its own sessions, separate from the browser on your computer. Once you sign in, your dot can use that session for later work until you sign out or the website requires another login. When available, <strong>Save to Passwords</strong> lets you optionally save the login. Using a saved login for a new sign-in requires your confirmation. See <a href="/codex/dots/computers-and-apps#sign-in-to-a-website">website sign-in</a>.</p><p>Some websites block cloud browsers or require extra verification. You can ask your dot to try a connected computer instead. This may create a separate task on that computer; it doesn’t transfer the cloud browser’s session.</p><h3 id="tasks-and-conversations" class="group flex items-center gap-1 mt-7 mb-2 6.31658 8.90236 6.7071 9.29289Z" fill="currentColor"></path></svg></button></h3><p>Your dot can use background agents, start new cloud threads, and create Work or Codex tasks on a connected computer. It can also continue existing local Codex tasks. For cloud coding work that needs your repository and setup, it can use a Codex cloud environment you’ve created.</p><p>Cloud threads appear as separate conversations in the desktop, web, and mobile apps, where you can review results and give further instructions. Local Codex tasks appear on the connected computer. You can keep talking to your dot while these tasks run.</p><p>In the desktop app, open your dot’s profile and select <strong>Activity</strong>, then open a task to inspect its progress, results, or requests for input. Your dot can check results and send follow-up instructions to tasks it created. See <a href="/codex/dots/tasks-and-memory#assigned-work">Tasks and memory</a> for where tasks run and how to continue them.</p><p>Connecting your computer lets your dot work with its tasks and files. It doesn’t give your dot access to every conversation in every app.</p><h3 id="permissions-and-approvals" class="group flex items-center gap-1 mt-7 mb-2 scroll-mt-[110px]"><span your dot what to change in the work already underway.</p><p>Ask your dot what it’s working on and what needs your input. In the desktop app, open its profile and use <strong>Activity</strong> to review delegated tasks. Ask it to list recurring work and confirm what’s scheduled.</p><p>Use <strong>Pause</strong> to stop your dot’s current main task. Stop delegated tasks in <strong>Activity</strong> and cancel recurring tasks in <strong>Scheduled</strong> separately. Ending a voice call doesn’t necessarily stop assigned work. See <a href="/codex/dots/controls#stop-work">Stop work</a>.</p><p>Review important results and their sources. Your dot can make mistakes, and stopping a task doesn’t undo actions it has already completed.</p><h3 id="ways-to-work-with-your-dot" class="group flex items-center gap-1 mt-7 mb-2 6.31658 8.90236 6.7071 9.29289Z" fill="currentColor"></path></svg></button></h3><p>Give your dot access to the relevant sources and tell it what to keep track of. For example:</p><ul>
<li><strong>Keep a sales proposal current.</strong> Share the proposal and customer requirements. As the requested seat count or terms change, have your dot update the figures, track outstanding security and technical reviews, and bring you the next decisions.</li>
<li><strong>Prepare content from each interview.</strong> Share the interview material and photos. Ask your dot to draft a caption, show notes, and clip ideas for review. You can refine the title or tone from your phone before publishing.</li>
<li><strong>Keep launch materials aligned with the product.</strong> Connect the launch channel and share the brief, deck, and approved visuals. Have your dot flag product changes that affect the campaign and prepare revised copy, slides, and speaker notes for your review.</li>
<li><strong>Update a study as results arrive.</strong> Share the study and new measurements. Have your dot update the comparison chart, explain where repeat results differ from the first batch, and draft a findings summary and proposed next tests for review.</li>
<li><strong>Follow up on software feedback.</strong> Connect the feedback source and code project. Ask your dot to investigate reported problems, such as a missing item in a sidebar, and prepare a fix for code review before merging.</li>
</ul><h2 id="access" class="group flex items-center gap-2 mt-7 mb-2 scroll-mt-[110px]"><span class="min-w-0">Access</span><button type="button" class="shrink-0 self-center inline-flex items-center class="_Content_1bpiz_147"><div class="_Message_1bpiz_166"><div class="_Description_1bpiz_176"><p><strong>For workspace admins:</strong> See <a href="/codex/enterprise/dots-admin-guide">Set up dots for work</a> for workspace setup, permissions, and security and governance guidance.</p></div></div></div></div></div><p>Dots are rolling out gradually. You may not see dots immediately, even if your plan is eligible.</p><ul>
<li><strong>Pro 100, Pro 200, and Pro 500:</strong> For users over 18 outside the European Economic Area, United Kingdom, and Switzerland.</li>
<li><strong>Business Premium:</strong> Rolling out worldwide.</li>
<li><strong>Enterprise:</strong> Rolling out worldwide. Dots are off by default and must be enabled by a workspace administrator.</li>
</ul><p>Conversations with your dot don’t count toward your ChatGPT usage limits. Tasks your dot starts or manages in Work or Codex count toward those products’ usage limits as usual. Your plan includes an allowance for deeper work, with extended limits for the first month after launch.</p><p>Create your dot in the desktop app or in ChatGPT on a desktop browser. After setup, use the same dot in the mobile app when the supporting update is available. Mobile web is not supported.</p><h2 id="reference" class="group flex items-center gap-2 mt-7 mb-2 scroll-mt-[110px]"><span class="min-w-0">Reference</span><button type="button" class="shrink-0
